title.zh: 卷340 列傳一百二十七 王杰 董诰 朱珪
title.en: Volume 340 Biographies 127: Wang Jie, Dong Gao, Zhu Gui
title.raw: 卷340 列傳一百二十七 王杰 董诰 朱珪

sentences.zh: 王杰，字偉人，陝西韓城人。

translations.literal: Wang Jie, style name Weiren, was a native of Hancheng in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jie, whose style was Weiren, came from Hancheng in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 以拔貢考銓藍田教諭，未任，遭父喪，貧甚，為書記以養母。

translations.literal: Having passed the examination as a selected tribute student, he was appointed through examination to be director of studies at Lantian, but before taking office he suffered his father's bereavement; being extremely poor, he worked as a secretary to support his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He qualified through the tribute-student channel for the post of director of studies at Lantian, but before he could assume it his father died. Penniless, he took work as a clerk to support his mother.

sentences.zh: 歷佐兩江總督尹繼善、江蘇巡撫陳宏謀幕，皆重之。

translations.literal: He successively served on the staffs of Yin Jishan, governor-general of the Two Jiangs, and Chen Hongmou, governor of Jiangsu; both held him in high esteem.
translations.idiomatic: He later served on the secretariats of Yin Jishan, governor-general of the Two Jiangs, and Chen Hongmou, governor of Jiangsu, and both men valued him highly.

sentences.zh: 初從武功孫景烈遊，講濂、洛、關、閩之學；

translations.literal: At first he associated with Sun Jinglie of Wugong, studying the learning of the Lian, Luo, Guan, and Min schools;
translations.idiomatic: Early on he studied under Sun Jinglie of Wugong in the Neo-Confucian traditions associated with Zhou Dunyi, the Cheng brothers, Zhang Zai, and Zhu Xi;

sentences.zh: 及見宏謀，學益進，自謂生平行己居官得力於此。

translations.literal: When he met Hongmou his learning advanced further; he said himself that in his conduct through life and in office he owed his strength to this.
translations.idiomatic: After he came to know Hongmou his studies advanced further still, and he would say that everything he achieved in private conduct and in public office he owed to this education.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十六年，成進士，殿試進呈卷列第三。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of the Qianlong reign he became a jinshi; in the palace examination his submitted paper ranked third.
translations.idiomatic: In 1761 he passed the metropolitan examination and took his jinshi degree; his palace-examination paper was ranked third among those presented to the throne.

sentences.zh: 高宗熟視字體如素識，以昔為尹繼善繕疏，曾邀宸賞，詢知人品，即拔置第一。

translations.literal: The Gaozong Emperor scrutinized his handwriting as if he had known it before; because in the past he had drafted memorials for Yin Jishan and had once won imperial approval, upon inquiry learning his character, he immediately raised him to first place.
translations.idiomatic: The Qianlong Emperor studied his calligraphy as if it were already familiar—he had once written drafts for Yin Jishan and won the emperor's notice—and on learning who he was, promptly placed him first.

sentences.zh: 及引見，風度凝然，上益喜。

translations.literal: When he was presented for audience, his bearing was composed and dignified; the emperor was all the more pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When he was brought before the throne, his deportment was grave and steady, which pleased the emperor still more.

sentences.zh: 又以陝人入本朝百餘年無大魁者，時值西陲戡定，魁選適得西人，御製詩以紀其事。

translations.literal: Moreover, for more than a century since the dynasty's founding no Shaanxi native had taken the highest honors; at this time the western frontier had just been pacified, and the top choice happened to be a westerner—the emperor composed a poem to commemorate the event.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, no native of Shaanxi had won first place in the examinations in over a century of the dynasty; with the western campaigns just concluded, the top graduate happened to come from the west, and the emperor wrote a verse to mark the occasion.

sentences.zh: 尋直南書房，屢司文柄。

translations.literal: Soon he was assigned to the Southern Imperial Study and repeatedly held charge of literary affairs at court.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon posted to the Southern Imperial Study and repeatedly oversaw literary and examination affairs.

sentences.zh: 五遷至內閣學士。

translations.literal: After five promotions he reached the post of Academician of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After five promotions he rose to Academician of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，授刑部侍郎，調吏部，擢左都御史。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year he was appointed vice minister of justice, transferred to the Board of Personnel, and promoted to censor-in-chief of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: In 1774 he was made vice minister of justice, transferred to the Board of Personnel, and promoted to left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 四十八年，丁母憂，即家擢兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year he entered mourning for his mother; while still at home he was promoted to minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: In 1783, while mourning his mother at home, he was promoted to minister of war.

sentences.zh: 車駕南巡，傑赴行在謝，上曰：「汝來甚好。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage made its southern tour, Jie went to the traveling palace to give thanks; the emperor said, "It is very good that you have come.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor toured the south, Jie went to the traveling palace to give thanks; the emperor said, "It is very good that you have come.

sentences.zh: 君臣久別，應知朕念汝。

translations.literal: Ruler and minister have been long parted; you ought to know that I have been thinking of you.
translations.idiomatic: After so long a separation between ruler and minister, you ought to know that I have been thinking of you.

sentences.zh: 然汝儒者，不欲奪汝情，歸終制可也。」

translations.literal: Yet you are a Confucian scholar; I do not wish to deprive you of your filial feeling—you may return and complete the full mourning period."
translations.idiomatic: Yet you are a Confucian scholar; I do not wish to deprive you of your filial duty—you may return and complete the full mourning period."

sentences.zh: 服闋，還朝。

translations.literal: When the mourning period ended, he returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning period ended, he returned to court.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，命為軍機大臣、上書房總師傅。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year he was appointed Grand Councilor and chief tutor of the Upper Imperial Study.
translations.idiomatic: In 1786 he was appointed Grand Councilor and chief tutor of the Upper Imperial Study.

sentences.zh: 次年，拜東閣大學士，管理禮部。

translations.literal: The following year he was made Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion and put in charge of the Board of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion and put in charge of the Board of Rites.

sentences.zh: 台灣、廓爾喀先後平，兩次圖形紫光閣，加太子太保。

translations.literal: Taiwan and Gorkha were pacified in succession; twice his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor, and he was given the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After Taiwan and Gorkha were pacified in succession, his portrait was twice placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor, and he was given the title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 傑在樞廷十餘年，事有可否，未嘗不委曲陳奏。

translations.literal: Jie served in the Grand Council for more than ten years; whenever a matter was feasible or not, he invariably submitted a circumspect memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Jie served on the Grand Council for more than ten years; whenever a policy was sound or unsound, he invariably submitted a careful, detailed memorial.

sentences.zh: 和珅勢方赫，事多擅決，同列隱忍不言，傑遇有不可，輒力爭。

translations.literal: Heshen's power was then at its height; he frequently decided matters on his own authority, and his colleagues endured it in silence—but whenever Jie encountered something unacceptable, he would contend vigorously.
translations.idiomatic: Heshen's power was then at its height; he often decided matters on his own, and his colleagues endured it in silence—but whenever Jie found something unacceptable, he would argue vigorously.

sentences.zh: 上知之深，和珅雖厭之而不能去。

translations.literal: The emperor knew this deeply; though Heshen disliked him, he could not remove him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew this well; though Heshen disliked him, he could not remove him.

sentences.zh: 傑每議政畢，默然獨坐。

translations.literal: After each policy discussion Jie would sit alone in silence.
translations.idiomatic: After each council session Jie would sit alone in silence.

sentences.zh: 一日，和珅執其手戲曰：「何柔荑乃爾！」

translations.literal: One day Heshen took his hand in jest and said, "How soft and delicate your hand is!"
translations.idiomatic: One day Heshen took his hand in jest and said, "What a soft, delicate hand you have!"

sentences.zh: 傑正色曰：「王杰手雖好，但不能要錢耳！」

translations.literal: Jie said sternly, "Wang Jie's hand may be fine, but it cannot take money!"
translations.idiomatic: Jie said sternly, "Wang Jie's hand may be fine, but it cannot take bribes!"

sentences.zh: 和珅赧然。

translations.literal: Heshen flushed with embarrassment.
translations.idiomatic: Heshen flushed with embarrassment.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，以足疾乞免軍機、書房及管理部事，允之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing, citing leg ailment he requested release from the Grand Council, the Imperial Study, and his administrative duties; permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In 1796, citing leg trouble, he asked to be relieved of his Grand Council post, his Imperial Study duties, and his ministerial responsibilities; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 有大事，上必諮詢，傑亦不時入告。

translations.literal: When great affairs arose the emperor invariably consulted him, and Jie also reported in from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: When major affairs arose the emperor always consulted him, and Jie also reported in from time to time.

sentences.zh: 時教匪方熾，傑疏言：「賊匪剿滅稽遲，由被賊災民窮無倚賴，地方官不能勞來安輯，以致脅從日眾，兵力日單而賊焰日熾。

translations.literal: At that time the sect rebels were raging fiercely; Jie memorialized: "The delay in exterminating the bandits is due to the fact that the people afflicted by the rebels are destitute and without support, and local officials cannot labor to bring them in and settle them, so that those coerced into joining grow daily in number, military strength grows daily weaker, and the rebels' flame grows daily fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the sect rebels were raging; Jie memorialized: "The delay in wiping out the rebels stems from the destitution of people in rebel-afflicted areas and local officials' failure to resettle and reassure them, so that those coerced into joining grow daily, military strength dwindles, and rebel power swells.

sentences.zh: 此時當安良民以解從賊之心，撫官兵以勵行間之氣。

translations.literal: At this time one should settle the good people to loosen the hearts of those following the rebels, and comfort officers and soldiers to encourage the spirit in the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: At this juncture we should reassure law-abiding civilians to loosen rebel sympathies, and support officers and troops to raise morale in the field.

sentences.zh: 三年之內，川、楚、秦、豫四省殺傷不下數百萬，其倖存而不從賊者，亦皆鋒鏑之餘，男不暇耕，女不暇織。

translations.literal: Within three years in the four provinces of Sichuan, Huguang, Shaanxi, and Henan the killed and wounded were no fewer than several millions; even those who survived and did not join the rebels were all remnants after blades and arrows—men had no leisure to plow, women no leisure to weave.
translations.idiomatic: Within three years in Sichuan, Huguang, Shaanxi, and Henan, casualties ran to millions; even survivors who did not join the rebels were left shattered by war—men could not farm, women could not weave.

sentences.zh: 若再計畝徵輸，甚至分外加派，胥吏因緣勒索，艱苦情形無由上達聖主之前。

translations.literal: If grain tax is again assessed by the mu and even extra levies are imposed by quota, clerks seize the opportunity to extort, and their bitter plight cannot reach the sage sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: If land tax is levied again by the mu, with extra assessments on top, and clerks extort at every turn, their suffering will never reach Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 祈將被賊地方錢糧蠲免，不令官吏舞弊重徵，有來歸者概勿窮治，賊勢或可漸孤矣。

translations.literal: I pray that grain and tax payments in rebel-afflicted areas be remitted, that officials not be allowed to cheat and levy heavily again, and that those who return be not prosecuted in every case—then rebel strength may gradually be isolated.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that taxes in rebel-afflicted areas be remitted, that officials be barred from fraud and heavy re-levying, and that returnees not be prosecuted wholesale—then the rebels may gradually be isolated.

sentences.zh: 至於用兵三載未即成功，實由將帥有所依恃，怠玩因循，非盡士卒之不用命也。

translations.literal: As for three years of campaigning without immediate success, it is truly because generals have something to rely on and are negligent and procrastinating—not entirely because the soldiers are disobedient.
translations.idiomatic: As for three years of war without swift victory, the fault lies with commanders who feel secure in their posts, grow negligent, and drag their feet—not wholly with soldiers' disobedience.

sentences.zh: 乞頒發諭旨，曲加憐恤，有驕惰不馴者，令經略概行撤回，或就近更調召募，申明紀律，鼓行勵戎，庶幾人有挾纊之歡，眾有成城之志。」

translations.literal: I beg that an edict be issued showing special compassion; those who are arrogant, lazy, and unruly should be withdrawn wholesale by the commander-in-chief, or replaced and recruited nearby; discipline should be made clear and the army encouraged—then perhaps men will have the joy of having padded garments in winter, and the multitude the will to defend the city together."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that an edict issue showing special care: arrogant, lazy, unruly commanders should be recalled wholesale by the commander-in-chief, or replaced with local recruits; discipline should be enforced and the army roused—then men may feel the warmth of winter clothing, and all the will to stand as one wall."

sentences.zh: 又言：「教匪之蔓延，其弊有二：一由統領之有名無實。

translations.literal: He also said: "The spread of the sect rebels has two abuses: first, the commander-in-chief is nominal in title but not in fact.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "The spread of the sect rebels has two root causes: first, the commander-in-chief is a name without real authority.

sentences.zh: 勒保雖為統領，而統兵大員名位相等，人人得專摺奏事，於是賊至則畏避不前，賊去則捏稱得勝。

translations.literal: Although Lebao was commander-in-chief, the great officers commanding troops were equal in rank and title; each could submit memorials on his own authority—thus when rebels came they shrank back and would not advance, and when rebels left they fabricated claims of victory.
translations.idiomatic: Although Lebao was commander-in-chief, the senior field commanders were equal in rank; each could memorialize the throne directly—so when rebels came they hung back, and when rebels left they claimed victories they had not won.

sentences.zh: 即如前歲賊竄興安，領兵大員有'匪已渡江五日，地方官並不禀報'之奏，此其畏避情形顯而易見。

translations.literal: For example, the year before last when rebels fled into Xing'an, a commanding officer memorialized that 'the bandits had crossed the river five days ago, yet local officials had not reported it'—their evasion is obvious.
translations.idiomatic: For example, when rebels fled into Xing'an the year before last, a field commander reported that 'the bandits had crossed the river five days ago, yet local officials had not reported it'—their timidity is plain.

sentences.zh: 又如去歲賊擾西安城南，殺傷數万，官兵既不近賊，撫臣一無設施；

translations.literal: Again, last year when rebels harassed south of Xi'an city, tens of thousands were killed and wounded; the officers and soldiers neither approached the rebels, and the governor took no measures at all;
translations.idiomatic: Again, last year when rebels raided south of Xi'an, tens of thousands were killed or wounded; the troops never closed with the enemy, and the governor did nothing;

sentences.zh: 探知賊去已遠，然後虛張聲勢，名為追賊，實未見賊。

translations.literal: after learning that the rebels had already gone far away, they then made a show of force in name pursuing the rebels, but in fact never saw them.
translations.idiomatic: only after learning the rebels were far away did they make a show of pursuit—called chasing bandits, yet never sighting them.

sentences.zh: 近聞張漢潮蔓延商、雒，高均德屯據洋縣，往來衝突，如入無人之境。

translations.literal: Recently it is heard that Zhang Hanchao has spread through Shang and Luo, Gao Junde has occupied and held Yang County, and they clash back and forth as if entering a realm with no one in it.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Zhang Hanchao has spread through Shang and Luo, Gao Junde holds Yang County, and they raid back and forth as if no one opposed them.

sentences.zh: 秦省如此，川省可知。

translations.literal: If Shaanxi is thus, Sichuan may be inferred.
translations.idiomatic: If Shaanxi is in this state, Sichuan may be imagined.

sentences.zh: 實由統領不專、賞罰不明之所致也。

translations.literal: This is truly caused by the commander-in-chief lacking sole authority and rewards and punishments being unclear.
translations.idiomatic: This truly stems from divided command and unclear rewards and punishments.

sentences.zh: 一由領兵大員專恃鄉勇。

translations.literal: Second, commanding officers rely exclusively on local militia.
translations.idiomatic: Second, field commanders rely exclusively on local militia.

sentences.zh: 鄉勇陣亡，無庸報部，人數可以虛捏；

translations.literal: When militia die in battle there is no need to report to the ministry, and numbers can be fabricated;
translations.idiomatic: Militia casualties need not be reported to the ministry, so head counts can be invented;

sentences.zh: 藉鄉勇為前陣，既可免官兵之傷亡，又可為異日之開銷，此所以耗國帑而無可稽核也。

translations.literal: Using militia as the front line both spares regular troops from casualties and provides expenses for future accounts—this is why the state treasury is drained with nothing to audit.
translations.idiomatic: Using militia as the front line spares regular troops and pads future expense accounts—hence the treasury drains away with nothing to audit.

sentences.zh: 臣以為軍務緊要，莫急於去鄉勇之名而為召募之實，蓋有五利：一，民窮無依，多半從賊，苟延性命，募而為兵，即有口糧，多一為兵之人，即少一從賊之人；

translations.literal: Your servant holds that in military affairs nothing is more urgent than removing the name of militia and making recruitment real; there are five benefits: first, the people are destitute and without support; most follow the rebels merely to prolong life—if recruited as soldiers they at once have rations; each man who becomes a soldier is one fewer who follows the rebels;
translations.idiomatic: Your servant holds that nothing in the war effort is more urgent than ending the militia fiction and recruiting real soldiers; there are five benefits: first, the destitute mostly join rebels merely to survive—recruit them as soldiers and they have rations at once; every man enlisted is one fewer rebel;

sentences.zh: 一，隔省徵調，曠日持久，就近召募，則旬日可得；

translations.literal: second, calling up troops from other provinces takes many days; recruiting nearby, they can be obtained in ten days;
translations.idiomatic: second, troops levied from distant provinces take weeks to arrive; local recruitment can fill ranks in ten days;

sentences.zh: 一，徵兵遠來，筋力已疲，召募之人，不須跋涉；

translations.literal: third, levied soldiers coming from afar are already weary in sinew and strength; recruited men need not trek long distances;
translations.idiomatic: third, levied troops arrive exhausted from the march; recruits need not travel far;

sentences.zh: 一，隔省之兵，水土不習，路徑不諳，就近之人，則不慮此；

translations.literal: fourth, soldiers from other provinces are unaccustomed to the water and soil and unfamiliar with the paths; local men need not fear this;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, out-of-province troops are unaccustomed to local climate and terrain; local recruits are not;

sentences.zh: 一，鄉勇勢不能敵，則逃散無從懲治，召募之兵退避，則有軍法。

translations.literal: fifth, when militia cannot match the enemy's strength they scatter in flight with no means of punishment; when recruited soldiers retreat, military law applies.
translations.idiomatic: fifth, militia who cannot stand their ground scatter without penalty; recruited soldiers who retreat face military law.

sentences.zh: 具此五利，何不增募，一鼓而殲賊？

translations.literal: With these five benefits, why not increase recruitment and destroy the rebels in one stroke?
translations.idiomatic: With these five advantages, why not recruit more men and crush the rebels in one blow?

sentences.zh: 如謂兵多費多，獨不思一萬兵食十月之糧，與十萬兵食一月之糧，其費相等而功可早奏也。」

translations.literal: If one says more troops mean more expense, has one not considered that ten thousand soldiers eating ten months' grain and one hundred thousand soldiers eating one month's grain cost the same, yet success can be reported sooner?"
translations.idiomatic: If one objects that more troops mean more cost, consider: ten thousand men fed for ten months costs the same as one hundred thousand fed for one month—but victory comes sooner."

sentences.zh: 疏入，並被採用。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, its recommendations were all adopted.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, its recommendations were adopted.

sentences.zh: 二年，復召直軍機，隨扈熱河。

translations.literal: In the second year he was again summoned to regular duty on the Grand Council and accompanied the emperor to Rehe.
translations.idiomatic: In 1797 he was again called back to regular Grand Council duty and accompanied the emperor to Rehe.

sentences.zh: 未幾，因腿疾，詔毋庸入直，先行回京。

translations.literal: Before long, because of leg ailment, an edict said he need not enter regular duty and might return first to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, because of leg trouble, he was excused from regular duty and sent back to the capital ahead of the court.

sentences.zh: 三年秋，川匪王三槐就擒，封賞樞臣，詔：「傑現雖未直軍機，軍興曾有贊畫功，並予優敘。」

translations.literal: In the autumn of the third year the Sichuan rebel Wang Sanhuai was captured; Grand Councilors were enfeoffed and rewarded; an edict said: "Although Jie is not now on regular Grand Council duty, in the military rise he once had merit in planning, and he too shall receive preferential commendation."
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of 1798 the Sichuan rebel Wang Sanhuai was captured; Grand Councilors were rewarded, and an edict said: "Although Jie is not now on regular Grand Council duty, he contributed to war planning and shall receive preferential commendation as well."

sentences.zh: 洎仁宗親政，傑為首輔，遇事持大體，竭誠進諫，上優禮之。

translations.literal: When the Renzong Emperor took personal rule, Jie became chief minister; in affairs he upheld the larger pattern, admonished with full sincerity, and the emperor treated him with special favor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiaqing Emperor took personal rule, Jie became chief minister; he upheld the larger principles in policy, admonished with full sincerity, and the emperor treated him with exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 五年，以衰病乞休，溫詔慰留，許扶杖入朝。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, citing age and illness he requested retirement; a warm edict comforted him and kept him on, permitting him to attend court leaning on a staff.
translations.idiomatic: In 1800, citing age and illness he asked to retire; a warm edict urged him to stay and allowed him to attend court with a walking staff.

sentences.zh: 七年，固請致仕，晉太子太傅，在籍食俸。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he firmly requested to retire from office; he was promoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and received salary while at home.
translations.idiomatic: In 1802 he firmly asked to retire; he was promoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and drew salary in his native place.

sentences.zh: 八年春，瀕行上疏，略謂：「各省虧空之弊，起於乾隆四十年以後，州縣營求餽送，以國帑為夤緣，上司受其挾制，彌補無期。

translations.literal: In the spring of the eighth year, on the eve of departure he submitted a memorial saying in summary: "The abuse of deficits in the provinces began after the fortieth year of Qianlong; districts and counties sought gifts and presents, used state funds as a ladder for connections, and superiors were constrained by them—making good the shortfall had no end in sight.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1803, on the eve of his departure he memorialized in summary: "Provincial deficits began after 1775: districts and counties solicited gifts, treated the treasury as a ladder for patronage, and superiors were held hostage—shortfalls could never be made good.

sentences.zh: 至嘉慶四年以後，大吏知尚廉節，州縣仍形拮据，由於苦樂不均，賢否不分，宜求整飭之法。

translations.literal: From the fourth year of Jiaqing onward, great officials knew to value integrity, yet districts and counties were still straitened, because hardship and ease were unevenly distributed and the worthy and unworthy were not distinguished—methods of rectification should be sought.
translations.idiomatic: Since 1799 senior officials have valued integrity, yet districts and counties remain strapped, because hardship and ease are uneven and the worthy and unworthy are not distinguished—rectification is needed.

sentences.zh: 又，舊制，驛丞專司驛站，無可誅求。

translations.literal: Moreover, under the old system post-station assistants were solely in charge of relay stations and had no means of extortion.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, under the old system post-station assistants managed relay stations alone and had no scope for extortion.

sentences.zh: 自裁歸州縣，濫支苛派，官民俱病。

translations.literal: Since the posts were abolished and returned to districts and counties, expenditures were abused and levies were harsh—officials and people alike suffered.
translations.idiomatic: Since those posts were abolished and their duties folded into districts and counties, spending has been abused and levies harsh—officials and people alike suffer.

sentences.zh: 宜先清驛站，以杜虧空。

translations.literal: Relay stations should first be cleared up to stop deficits.
translations.idiomatic: Relay stations should be put in order first to stop deficits.

sentences.zh: 今當軍務告竣，朝廷勤求治理，無大於此二者。

translations.literal: Now that military affairs are concluded, the court diligently seeks good governance—nothing is greater than these two matters.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the war is ending and the court is striving for good governance, nothing matters more than these two reforms.

sentences.zh: 請睿裁獨斷，以挽積重之勢。」

translations.literal: I pray Your sagely judgment may decide alone and turn back this long-accumulated trend."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to decide decisively and reverse this long-accumulated trend."

sentences.zh: 所言切中時弊，上嘉納之。

translations.literal: What he said struck at the abuses of the time; the emperor commended and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: His words struck at the abuses of the day; the emperor commended and accepted them.

sentences.zh: 陛辭日，賜高宗御用玉鳩杖、御製詩二章，以寵其行，有云：「直道一身立廊廟，清風兩袖返韓城。」

translations.literal: On the day of his farewell audience he was given the Gaozong Emperor's personal jade dove staff and two imperial poems to honor his departure; one line read: "With upright conduct he stood alone in the hall of state; with clear wind in both sleeves he returns to Hancheng."
translations.idiomatic: On the day of his farewell audience he received the Qianlong Emperor's personal jade dove staff and two imperial poems to honor his departure; one line read: "With upright conduct he stood alone in the hall of state; with clear wind in both sleeves he returns to Hancheng."

sentences.zh: 時論謂足盡其生平。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion said this fully summed up his life.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary opinion held that this fully summed up his life.

sentences.zh: 既歸，歲時頒賞不絕，每有陳奏，上輒親批答，語如家人。

translations.literal: After he returned home, seasonal gifts and rewards never ceased; whenever he memorialized, the emperor personally wrote replies in a tone like family.
translations.idiomatic: After he returned home, seasonal gifts never ceased; whenever he memorialized, the emperor personally wrote replies in the tone of family conversation.

sentences.zh: 九年，傑與妻程並年八十，命巡撫方維甸齎御​​製詩、額、珍物，於生日就賜其家。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Jie and his wife Lady Cheng were both eighty; the emperor ordered Governor Fang Weidian to carry imperial poems, a plaque, and precious objects and bestow them at their home on their birthday.
translations.idiomatic: In 1804 Jie and his wife Lady Cheng both turned eighty; the emperor ordered Governor Fang Weidian to bring imperial poems, a plaque, and precious gifts to their home on their birthday.

sentences.zh: 傑詣闕謝，明年正月，卒於京邸。

translations.literal: Jie went to the palace to give thanks; in the first month of the following year he died at his residence in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Jie went to court to give thanks; in the first month of the following year he died at his residence in the capital.

sentences.zh: 上悼惜，賜金治喪，贈太子太師，祀賢良祠，諡文端。

translations.literal: The emperor mourned him with regret, granted gold for the funeral, posthumously gave him the title Senior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, enshrined him in the Shrine of Worthies, and gave the posthumous name Wenduan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him, granted gold for the funeral, posthumously made him Senior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, enshrined him in the Shrine of Worthies, and gave the posthumous name Wenduan.

sentences.zh: 傑體不逾中人，和靄近情，而持守剛正，歷事兩朝，以忠直結主知。

translations.literal: Jie's physique did not exceed that of an average man; he was kindly and approachable, yet upheld firm integrity; serving two reigns, he won the sovereign's trust through loyalty and uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: Jie was of no more than average stature, kindly and approachable, yet steadfastly upright; serving two reigns, he won the sovereign's trust through loyalty and integrity.

sentences.zh: 當致仕未行，會有陳德於禁城驚犯乘輿，急趨朝請對曰：「德庖廚賤役，安敢妄蓄逆謀？

translations.literal: When he had not yet retired, there occurred Chen De's startling assault on the imperial carriage within the Forbidden City; Jie hurried to court and requested an audience, saying: "De is a lowly kitchen servant—how would he dare harbor rebellious designs?
translations.idiomatic: Before he had retired, Chen De shocked the court by assaulting the imperial carriage within the Forbidden City; Jie hurried to court and said: "De is a lowly kitchen servant—how could he harbor treasonous designs on his own?

sentences.zh: 此必有元姦大憝主使行明張差之事，當除肘腋之患。」

translations.literal: There must be a chief villain behind him directing this, as in the clear case of Zhang Cha—the trouble at the elbow and armpit must be removed."
translations.idiomatic: There must be a chief villain behind him, as in the Zhang Cha affair—this threat at the emperor's very side must be uprooted."

sentences.zh: 至十八年林清逆黨之變，上思其言，特賜祭焉。

translations.literal: By the eighteenth year, when Lin Qing's rebel faction rose, the emperor recalled his words and specially granted sacrificial rites.
translations.idiomatic: By 1813, when Lin Qing's rebels struck, the emperor recalled his words and specially granted sacrificial rites in his honor.

sentences.zh: 孫篤，道光二年進士，歷編修、御史，出為汀州知府、廣東督糧道，署鹽運使。

translations.literal: His grandson Du, a jinshi in the second year of Daoguang, served successively as compiler, censor, prefect of Tingzhou, grain superintendent of Guangdong, and acting salt controller.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Du, a jinshi in 1822, served as compiler, censor, prefect of Tingzhou, Guangdong grain superintendent, and acting salt controller.

sentences.zh: 時林則徐為按察使，治海防，甚倚之。

translations.literal: At that time Lin Zexu was provincial judge and managed coastal defense; he relied on him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Lin Zexu was provincial judge overseeing coastal defense and relied on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 募廣州遊手精壯者備守禦，以機敏稱。

translations.literal: He recruited sturdy idlers of Guangzhou for defense and was known for quick wit.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited sturdy Guangzhou idlers for coastal defense and was known for quick resourcefulness.

sentences.zh: 擢山東布政使，署巡撫。

translations.literal: He was promoted to provincial administration commissioner of Shandong and acted as governor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to provincial administration commissioner of Shandong and served as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 失察家人、屬官受賂，連降罷職歸，襄理西安城工。

translations.literal: For failure to detect that his household and subordinate officials took bribes, he was demoted repeatedly, dismissed, and returned home, then assisted in managing Xi'an city works.
translations.idiomatic: For failing to detect bribery by his household and subordinates, he was repeatedly demoted, dismissed, and sent home, then helped manage Xi'an city works.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈布政使銜。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was given the rank of provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously given the rank of provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 董誥，字蔗林，浙江富陽人，尚書邦達子。

translations.literal: Dong Gao, style name Zhelin, was a native of Fuyang in Zhejiang, son of Minister Dong Bangda.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Gao, whose style was Zhelin, came from Fuyang in Zhejiang; he was the son of Minister Dong Bangda.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十八年進士，殿試進呈卷列第三，高宗因大臣子，改二甲第一。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the twenty-eighth year of Qianlong; in the palace examination his submitted paper ranked third, but because he was a great minister's son the Gaozong Emperor changed him to first in the second class.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi in 1763; his palace-examination paper ranked third, but because he was a senior minister's son the Qianlong Emperor placed him first in the second class instead.

sentences.zh: 選庶吉士，即預修國史、三通、皇朝禮器圖。

translations.literal: He was selected as a Hanlin bachelor and at once took part in compiling the national history, the Three Comprehensive Encyclopedias, and the Illustrated Rites of the Dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Selected as a Hanlin bachelor, he at once joined work on the national history, the Three Comprehensive Encyclopedias, and the Illustrated Rites of the Dynasty.

sentences.zh: 散館，授編修。

translations.literal: When the Hanlin term ended he was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: When his Hanlin term ended he was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，命入懋勤殿寫金字經為皇太后祝嘏。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he was ordered to enter the Hall of Diligent Study to write a gold-letter sutra to pray for the empress dowager's longevity.
translations.idiomatic: In 1767 he was ordered to the Hall of Diligent Study to copy a gold-letter sutra for the empress dowager's birthday blessings.

sentences.zh: 次年，大考翰詹，因寫經未與試，特加一級。

translations.literal: The following year, in the great examination of Hanlin and Hanlin bachelors, because he had been copying the sutra and did not take the test, he was specially given one promotion.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, in the triennial Hanlin examination, he was excused because of the sutra work and given a special promotion.

sentences.zh: 尋擢中允，丁父憂。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to middle attendant and entered mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to middle attendant, then entered mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 三十六年，服闋，入直南書房。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year, when mourning ended, he entered regular duty in the Southern Imperial Study.
translations.idiomatic: In 1771, when mourning ended, he took up regular duty in the Southern Imperial Study.

sentences.zh: 初，邦達善畫，受高宗知。

translations.literal: At first Bangda was skilled at painting and won the Gaozong Emperor's notice.
translations.idiomatic: Bangda had been skilled at painting and won the Qianlong Emperor's notice.

sentences.zh: 誥承家學，繼為侍從，書畫亦被宸賞，尤以奉職恪勤為上所眷注。

translations.literal: Gao inherited the family learning and in turn became an attendant at court; his calligraphy and painting also won imperial approval, but above all his dutiful and diligent service won the emperor's special regard.
translations.idiomatic: Gao inherited the family tradition and in turn became a court attendant; his calligraphy and painting also won imperial praise, but above all his dutiful service won the emperor's special regard.

sentences.zh: 累遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: After repeated promotions he reached Grand Secretary of the Inner Cabinet.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated promotions he rose to Grand Secretary of the Inner Cabinet.

sentences.zh: 四十年，擢工部侍郎，調戶部，歷署吏、刑兩部侍郎，兼管樂部。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year he was promoted to vice minister of works, transferred to the Board of Revenue, successively acted as vice minister of the Boards of Personnel and Justice, and concurrently managed the Board of Rites' music section.
translations.idiomatic: In 1775 he was made vice minister of works, transferred to the Board of Revenue, served in turn as acting vice minister of the Boards of Personnel and Justice, and concurrently managed the music section of the Board of Rites.

sentences.zh: 充四庫館副總裁，接辦全書薈要，命輯滿洲源流考。

translations.literal: He served as deputy chief compiler of the Siku Library project, took over compilation of the Essentials of the Complete Library, and was ordered to compile an Investigation of Manchu Origins.
translations.idiomatic: He served as deputy chief compiler of the Siku Library, took over the Essentials of the Complete Library, and was ordered to compile an Investigation of Manchu Origins.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，命為軍機大臣。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year he was appointed Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1779 he was appointed Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，加太子少保，擢戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year he was given the title Junior Vice Guardian of the Heir Apparent and promoted to minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In 1787 he was made Junior Vice Guardian of the Heir Apparent and promoted to minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 台灣、廓爾喀先後底定，並列功臣，圖形紫光閣。

translations.literal: Taiwan and Gorkha were pacified in succession; he was listed among the meritorious officials and his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: After Taiwan and Gorkha were pacified in succession, he was listed among the meritorious officials and his portrait was placed in the Hall of Purple Splendor.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，授受禮成，詔硃珪來京，將畀以閣務，仁宗賀以詩。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing, when the succession rites were completed, an edict summoned Zhu Gui to the capital to be given Grand Secretariat duties; the Renzong Emperor congratulated him with a poem.
translations.idiomatic: In 1796, when the succession rites were completed, an edict summoned Zhu Gui to the capital for a Grand Secretariat post; the Jiaqing Emperor congratulated him with a poem.

sentences.zh: 屬稿未竟，和珅取白高宗曰：「嗣皇帝欲市恩於師傅。」

translations.literal: The draft was not yet finished when Heshen reported to the Gaozong Emperor, saying, "The heir apparent wishes to curry favor with his tutor."
translations.idiomatic: Before the draft was finished, Heshen told the Qianlong Emperor, "The heir apparent wishes to curry favor with his tutor."

sentences.zh: 高宗色動，顧誥曰：「汝在軍機、刑部久，是於律意云何？」

translations.literal: The Gaozong Emperor's expression changed; he turned to Gao and said, "You have long served on the Grand Council and at the Board of Justice—what is your view of the intent of the law?"
translations.idiomatic: The Qianlong Emperor's expression changed; he turned to Gao and said, "You have long served on the Grand Council and at the Board of Justice—what is your view of this under the law?"

sentences.zh: 誥叩頭曰：「聖主無過言。」

translations.literal: Gao kowtowed and said, "The sage sovereign speaks without fault."
translations.idiomatic: Gao kowtowed and said, "The sage sovereign speaks without fault."

sentences.zh: 高宗默然良久，曰：「汝大臣也，善為朕輔導之。」

translations.literal: The Gaozong Emperor was silent a long while, then said, "You are a great minister—guide him well for me."
translations.idiomatic: The Qianlong Emperor was silent a long while, then said, "You are a great minister—guide him well for me."

sentences.zh: 乃以他事罷珪之召。

translations.literal: Then on another pretext Gui's summons was canceled.
translations.idiomatic: Then on another pretext Gui's summons was canceled.

sentences.zh: 時大學士懸缺久，難其人。

translations.literal: At that time the post of Grand Secretary had long been vacant; a suitable man was hard to find.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Grand Secretary post had long been vacant; a suitable man was hard to find.

sentences.zh: 高宗謂劉墉、紀昀、彭元瑞三人皆資深，墉遇事模棱，元瑞以不檢獲愆，昀讀書多而不明理，惟誥在直勤勉，超拜東閣大學士，明詔宣示，俾三人加愧勵焉。

translations.literal: The Gaozong Emperor said that Liu Yong, Ji Yun, and Peng Yuanrui were all senior in service: Liu Yong was equivocal in affairs; Peng Yuanrui had been censured for lack of restraint; Ji Yun read much but did not understand principle—only Gao, diligent in regular duty, was promoted over their heads to Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, with an explicit edict proclaiming this to make the three feel still greater shame and spur.
translations.idiomatic: The Qianlong Emperor said Liu Yong, Ji Yun, and Peng Yuanrui were all senior: Liu Yong was equivocal in affairs; Peng Yuanrui had been censured for misconduct; Ji Yun read widely but lacked sound judgment—only Gao, diligent in regular duty, was promoted over their heads to Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, with an explicit edict to shame and spur the three.

sentences.zh: 命總理禮部，仍兼管戶部事。

translations.literal: He was ordered to take general charge of the Board of Rites while still concurrently managing affairs of the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to take general charge of the Board of Rites while still managing the Board of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 二年，丁生母憂，特賜陀羅經被，遣御前侍衛、額駙丰紳殷德奠醊。

translations.literal: In the second year he entered mourning for his birth mother; he was specially given a dharaṇī sutra quilt, and an imperial bodyguard and imperial son-in-law Fengshen Yinde were sent to offer libations.
translations.idiomatic: In 1797 he entered mourning for his birth mother; he was specially given a dharaṇī sutra quilt, and an imperial bodyguard and imperial son-in-law Fengshen Yinde were sent to offer libations.

sentences.zh: 誥既以喪歸，川、楚兵事方亟，高宗欲召之，每見大臣，數問；

translations.literal: After Gao returned home in mourning, military affairs in Sichuan and Huguang were urgent; the Gaozong Emperor wished to summon him and whenever he saw great ministers asked repeatedly;
translations.idiomatic: After Gao returned home in mourning, the Sichuan and Huguang campaigns were urgent; the Qianlong Emperor wished to recall him and asked repeatedly whenever he saw senior ministers;

sentences.zh: 「董誥何時來？」

translations.literal: "When will Dong Gao come?"
translations.idiomatic: "When will Dong Gao come?"

sentences.zh: 逾年，葬母畢，詣京師，和珅遏不上聞。

translations.literal: After more than a year, when his mother's burial was complete, he went to the capital; Heshen blocked the report from reaching the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year, when his mother's burial was complete, he went to the capital; Heshen blocked the report from reaching the emperor.

sentences.zh: 會駕出，誥於道旁謝恩，高宗見之，喜甚，命暫署刑部尚書，素服視事，不預典禮，專辦秋讞及軍營紀略，且曰：「誥守制已逾小祥，不得已用人之苦心，眾當共諒。」

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage went out, Gao gave thanks by the roadside; the Gaozong Emperor saw him and was greatly pleased, ordering him temporarily to act as minister of justice, to handle affairs in plain mourning dress without taking part in ceremonies, and to specialize in autumn assizes and military camp summaries, saying: "Gao's mourning observance has already passed the lesser anniversary; the bitter necessity of using a man—everyone should understand together."
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage went out, Gao gave thanks by the roadside; the Qianlong Emperor saw him and was greatly pleased, ordering him temporarily to act as minister of justice in plain mourning dress, excluding him from ceremonies but putting him in charge of autumn assizes and military summaries, and saying: "Gao's mourning has already passed the lesser anniversary; the bitter necessity of using him—everyone should understand."

sentences.zh: 尋以王三槐就擒，與軍機大臣同被議敘。

translations.literal: Soon, because Wang Sanhuai was captured, he received commendation along with the Grand Councilors.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, when Wang Sanhuai was captured, he received commendation along with the Grand Councilors.

sentences.zh: 四年春，高宗崩，和珅伏誅，命誥复直軍機，晉太子太保。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year the Gaozong Emperor died; Heshen was executed; Gao was ordered to resume regular Grand Council duty and was promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1799 the Qianlong Emperor died; Heshen was executed; Gao was ordered back to regular Grand Council duty and promoted to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 既，服闋，授文華殿大學士，兼刑部尚書如故。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was made Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory and continued as before as minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was made Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory while continuing as minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 高宗山陵禮成，命題神主，晉太子太傅。

translations.literal: When the Gaozong Emperor's mausoleum rites were completed, he was ordered to compose the spirit tablet inscription and was promoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qianlong Emperor's mausoleum rites were completed, he was ordered to compose the spirit-tablet inscription and was promoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 七年，三省教匪平，予騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the sect rebels in the three provinces were pacified; he was given a hereditary post as commandant of cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In 1802 the sect rebels in the three provinces were pacified; he was given a hereditary post as commandant of cavalry.

sentences.zh: 十二年，高宗實錄告成，詔以誥在館八年，始終其事，特加優獎，賜其父邦達入祀賢良祠。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the Veritable Records of the Gaozong Emperor were completed; an edict said that because Gao had been in the project office eight years and had seen it through from start to finish, he received special commendation and his father Bangda was granted enshrinement in the Shrine of Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: In 1807 the Qianlong Veritable Records were completed; an edict noted that Gao had spent eight years in the project office and seen it through from start to finish, gave him special commendation, and granted his father Bangda enshrinement in the Shrine of Worthies.

sentences.zh: 十四年，萬壽慶典，晉太子太師。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, at the longevity celebration, he was promoted to Senior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In 1809, at the longevity celebration, he was promoted to Senior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 充上書房總師傅。

translations.literal: He served as chief tutor of the Upper Imperial Study.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief tutor of the Upper Imperial Study.

sentences.zh: 十七年，晉太保。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was promoted to Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: In 1812 he was promoted to Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 十八年，扈從秋狝。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he accompanied the autumn hunt at Rehe.
translations.idiomatic: In 1813 he accompanied the autumn hunt at Rehe.

sentences.zh: 林清逆黨突入禁城，時回鑾，中途聞變，有議俟調大兵成列而後進者，誥曰：「是滋亂也，獻俘者行至矣！」

translations.literal: Lin Qing's rebel faction suddenly entered the Forbidden City; at that time the court was returning from Rehe; midway they heard of the disturbance; some proposed waiting until large forces were assembled in formation before advancing—Gao said, "That would only encourage disorder; those who present captives are already on the road!"
translations.idiomatic: Lin Qing's rebels suddenly entered the Forbidden City; the court was returning from Rehe and heard of the disturbance en route; some proposed waiting until large forces were assembled before advancing—Gao said, "That would only encourage disorder; the captors are already on their way!"

sentences.zh: 即日扈駕進次，人心乃定。

translations.literal: That same day he accompanied the imperial carriage to advance to the next stop, and popular sentiment was calmed.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he accompanied the imperial carriage forward, and public morale steadied.

sentences.zh: 窮治邪教，誥謂：「燒香祈福，愚民無知，率所常有。

translations.literal: In the thorough prosecution of heterodox sects, Gao said, "Burning incense to pray for blessings is what ignorant common people do without knowledge—it is what they always do.
translations.idiomatic: In prosecuting heterodox sects, Gao said, "Burning incense to pray for blessings is what ignorant common people routinely do.

sentences.zh: 惟從逆者不可貸。」

translations.literal: Only those who followed rebellion cannot be pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: Only those who joined rebellion cannot be pardoned."

sentences.zh: 凡論上，皆以是定讞。

translations.literal: In every case submitted for judgment, verdicts were fixed by this principle.
translations.idiomatic: In every case submitted for judgment, verdicts were fixed by this principle.

sentences.zh: 林清既誅，滑縣逆匪尋平，論功，迭被優敘，賜子淳為郎中。

translations.literal: After Lin Qing was executed, the rebels of Hua County were soon pacified; in accounting merit Gao received repeated preferential commendation, and his son Chun was given the post of director in a ministry.
translations.idiomatic: After Lin Qing was executed, the Hua County rebels were soon pacified; in accounting merit Gao received repeated preferential commendation, and his son Chun was given a directorship in a ministry.

sentences.zh: 二十年，因病請致政，溫詔慰留，改管兵部。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, citing illness he requested retirement from office; a warm edict comforted him and kept him on, changing his charge to the Board of War.
translations.idiomatic: In 1815, citing illness he asked to retire; a warm edict urged him to stay and transferred his charge to the Board of War.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復命管刑部。

translations.literal: Before long he was again ordered to manage the Board of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was again ordered to manage the Board of Justice.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，再疏乞休，許致仕食全俸。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he again memorialized begging to retire; permission was granted to retire and draw full salary.
translations.idiomatic: In 1818 he again memorialized to retire; permission was granted to retire on full salary.

sentences.zh: 是年十月，卒，贈太傅。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of that year he died; posthumously he was given the title Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of that year he died; posthumously he was given the title Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 上親奠，入祀賢良祠，賜金治喪，御製詩輓之，嘉其父子歷事三朝，未嘗增置一畝之田、一椽之屋，命刻詩於墓，以彰忠藎。

translations.literal: The emperor personally offered libations; he was enshrined in the Shrine of Worthies; gold was granted for the funeral; an imperial poem mourned him, praising father and son for serving three reigns without ever adding a single mu of land or a single rafter of house; the emperor ordered the poem carved on the tomb to manifest their loyalty and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally offered libations; he was enshrined in the Shrine of Worthies; gold was granted for the funeral; an imperial elegy praised father and son for serving three reigns without ever adding a single mu of land or a single beam of house; the emperor ordered the poem carved on the tomb to honor their loyalty and integrity.

sentences.zh: 諡文恭。

translations.literal: His posthumous name was Wengong.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Wengong.

sentences.zh: 誥直軍機先後四十年，熟於朝章故事，有以諮者，無不悉。

translations.literal: Gao served on regular Grand Council duty for forty years in all; he was versed in court regulations and precedents—whoever consulted him found nothing he did not know thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: Gao served on regular Grand Council duty for forty years in all; he knew court regulations and precedents inside out—whoever consulted him found nothing he did not know.

sentences.zh: 凡所獻納皆面陳，未嘗用奏牘。

translations.literal: Whatever he presented was always stated in person; he never used written memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever he presented he always stated in person; he never used written memorials.

sentences.zh: 當和珅用事，與王杰支柱其間，獨居深念，行處幾失常度，卒贊仁宗殲除大憝。

translations.literal: When Heshen held power, he and Wang Jie propped up affairs between them; alone he thought deeply, and in walking about he nearly lost normal composure—yet in the end he assisted the Renzong Emperor in destroying the great villain.
translations.idiomatic: When Heshen held power, he and Wang Jie held the line between them; alone he brooded deeply, and in walking about he nearly lost his composure—yet in the end he helped the Jiaqing Emperor destroy the great villain.

sentences.zh: 及林清之變，獨持鎮定，尤為時稱雲。

translations.literal: At the time of Lin Qing's disturbance he alone maintained composure, which contemporaries especially praised.
translations.idiomatic: At Lin Qing's disturbance he alone kept his composure, which contemporaries especially praised.

sentences.zh: 硃珪，字石君，順天大興人。

translations.literal: Zhu Gui, style name Shijun, was a native of Daxing in Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Gui, whose style was Shijun, came from Daxing in Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 先世居蕭山，自父文炳始遷籍。

translations.literal: His ancestors lived in Xiaoshan; from his father Wenbing the family transferred its registration.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors lived in Xiaoshan; his father Wenbing was the first to transfer the family's registration.

sentences.zh: 文炳官盩厔知縣，曾受經於大學士硃軾。

translations.literal: Wenbing served as magistrate of Zhouzhi and had once studied the classics under Grand Secretary Zhu Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbing served as magistrate of Zhouzhi and had studied the classics under Grand Secretary Zhu Shi.

sentences.zh: 珪少傳軾學，與兄筠同鄉舉，並負時譽。

translations.literal: Gui in youth inherited Shi's learning; with his elder brother Yun he passed the provincial examination in the same year, and both enjoyed contemporary renown.
translations.idiomatic: Gui in youth inherited Shi's learning; he and his elder brother Yun passed the provincial examination together and both enjoyed contemporary renown.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十三年成進士，年甫十八，選庶吉士，散館授編修。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Qianlong he became a jinshi at only eighteen, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and when the term ended was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In 1748 he became a jinshi at only eighteen, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and when his term ended was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 數遇典禮，撰進文冊。

translations.literal: He repeatedly encountered great ceremonies and drafted the submitted ceremonial documents.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly took part in great ceremonies and drafted the submitted ceremonial documents.

sentences.zh: 高宗重其學行，累遷侍讀學士。

translations.literal: The Gaozong Emperor valued his learning and conduct; after repeated promotions he reached reader-in-waiting of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: The Qianlong Emperor valued his learning and conduct; after repeated promotions he rose to reader-in-waiting of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，出為福建糧驛道。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he went out as grain and courier intendant of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In 1760 he was posted outside the capital as grain and courier intendant of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 擢按察使，治獄平恕，以父憂去。

translations.literal: He was promoted to provincial judge; in handling cases he was fair and lenient, and left office on his father's bereavement.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to provincial judge; in handling cases he was fair and lenient, and left office to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，補湖北按察使。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he was appointed provincial judge of Hubei to fill a vacancy.
translations.idiomatic: In 1767 he was appointed provincial judge of Hubei to fill a vacancy.

sentences.zh: 會緬甸用兵，以部署驛務詳慎，被褒獎。

translations.literal: When Burma was at war, because his deployment of relay-station affairs was detailed and careful, he received commendation.
translations.idiomatic: During the Burma campaign, his careful deployment of relay-station affairs won commendation.

sentences.zh: 調山西，就遷布政使，署巡撫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Shanxi, then promoted in place to provincial administration commissioner and acted as governor.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Shanxi, promoted in place to provincial administration commissioner, and served as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 疏請歸化、綏遠二城穀二萬餘石搭放兵糧，以省採買、免紅朽；

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting that more than twenty thousand shi of grain in the two cities of Guihua and Suiyuan be lent out for military rations to save purchasing and avoid spoilage;
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that more than twenty thousand shi of grain in Guihua and Suiyuan be lent for military rations to save purchasing and avoid spoilage;

sentences.zh: 又免土默特蒙古私墾罪，以所墾牧地三千餘頃，許附近兵民認耕納租，歲六千餘兩，增官兵公費；

translations.literal: he also remitted the crime of unauthorized cultivation by Tumed Mongols, and of the more than three thousand qing of pasture land thus cultivated permitted nearby soldiers and civilians to claim fields and pay rent, yielding more than six thousand taels yearly to increase public expenses of officers and soldiers;
translations.idiomatic: he also remitted penalties for unauthorized cultivation by Tumed Mongols, and of the more than three thousand qing thus opened permitted nearby soldiers and civilians to farm and pay rent, yielding more than six thousand taels yearly for officers' and soldiers' public expenses;

sentences.zh: 又太僕寺牧地苦寒，改徵折色，以便民除弊；

translations.literal: further, because pasture lands of the Court of the Imperial Stud were bitterly cold, he changed collection to cash payment to benefit the people and remove abuses;
translations.idiomatic: further, because the Court of the Imperial Stud's pasture lands were bitterly cold, he changed collection to cash payment to benefit the people and remove abuses;

sentences.zh: 皆下部議行。

translations.literal: all were referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: all were referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.

sentences.zh: 珪方正，為同僚所不便，按察使黃檢奏劾讀書廢事。

translations.literal: Gui was upright and square, which made colleagues uncomfortable; provincial judge Huang Jian memorialized impeaching him for reading books and neglecting affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was upright, which made colleagues uncomfortable; provincial judge Huang Jian memorialized impeaching him for reading books and neglecting affairs.

sentences.zh: 四十年，召入覲，改授侍講學士，直上書房，侍仁宗學。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year he was summoned to audience, transferred to expositor-in-waiting of the Hanlin Academy, entered regular duty in the Upper Imperial Study, and attended the Renzong Emperor's studies.
translations.idiomatic: In 1775 he was summoned to audience, made expositor-in-waiting of the Hanlin Academy, entered regular duty in the Upper Imperial Study, and tutored the Jiaqing Emperor.

sentences.zh: 四十四年，典福建鄉試。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year he presided over the Fujian provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1779 he presided over the Fujian provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 次年，督福建學政。

translations.literal: The following year he supervised education in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he supervised education in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 瀕行，上五箴於仁宗：曰養心，曰敬身，曰勤業，曰虛己，曰致誠。

translations.literal: On the eve of departure he presented five admonitions to the Renzong Emperor: on nurturing the mind, on revering the person, on diligent endeavor, on emptying the self, and on attaining sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of departure he presented five admonitions to the Jiaqing Emperor: on nurturing the mind, revering the person, diligent endeavor, emptying the self, and attaining sincerity.

sentences.zh: 仁宗力行之，後親政，嘗置左右。

translations.literal: The Renzong Emperor practiced them vigorously; after taking personal rule he kept them at hand.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiaqing Emperor practiced them vigorously; after taking personal rule he kept them at hand.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，擢禮部侍郎，典江南鄉試，督浙江學政。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year he was promoted to vice minister of rites, presided over the Jiangnan provincial examination, and supervised education in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1786 he was made vice minister of rites, presided over the Jiangnan provincial examination, and supervised education in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 還朝，調兵部。

translations.literal: On returning to court he was transferred to the Board of War.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he was transferred to the Board of War.

sentences.zh: 五十五年，典會試。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fifth year he presided over the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1790 he presided over the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 出為安徽巡撫。

translations.literal: He went out as governor of Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as governor of Anhui.

sentences.zh: 皖北水災，馳驛往賑，攜僕數人，與村民同舟渡，賑宿州、泗州、碭山、靈壁、五河、盱眙餘災，輕者貸以糧種。

translations.literal: When northern Anhui suffered flood disaster, he rushed by post-horse to give relief, taking only a few servants and crossing in the same boat with villagers; he relieved remaining disaster in Suzhou, Sizhou, Dangshan, Lingbi, Wuhe, and Xuyi, and to lighter cases lent grain seed.
translations.idiomatic: When northern Anhui suffered floods, he rushed by post-horse to give relief with only a few servants, crossing in the same boats as villagers; he relieved remaining disaster in Suzhou, Sizhou, Dangshan, Lingbi, Wuhe, and Xuyi, and lent grain seed to lighter cases.

sentences.zh: 築決堤，展春賑，並躬蒞其事，民無流亡。

translations.literal: He repaired breached dikes, extended spring relief, and personally oversaw the work; the people did not flee.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired breached dikes, extended spring relief, and personally oversaw the work; the people did not flee.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，調廣東。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year he was transferred to Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In 1794 he was transferred to Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 尋署兩廣總督，授左都御史、兵部尚書，仍留巡撫任。

translations.literal: Soon he acted as governor-general of the Two Guangs, was given the posts of left censor-in-chief and minister of war, and still retained the governorship.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he acted as governor-general of the Two Guangs, was made left censor-in-chief and minister of war, and still retained the governorship.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，授總督，兼署巡撫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing he was appointed governor-general and concurrently acted as governor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1796 he was appointed governor-general and concurrently acted as governor.

sentences.zh: 珪初以文學受知，洎出任疆寄，負時望，將大用。

translations.literal: Gui had first won notice through literary accomplishment; when he went out to hold frontier responsibility he bore contemporary expectations and was about to be greatly employed.
translations.idiomatic: Gui had first won notice through literary accomplishment; when he took up frontier office he bore high expectations and was on the verge of great promotion.

sentences.zh: 和珅忌之，授受禮成，珪進頌冊，因加指摘，高宗曰：「陳善納誨，師傅之職宜爾，非汝所知也。」

translations.literal: Heshen envied him; when the succession rites were completed Gui presented a eulogy booklet and was therefore criticized; the Gaozong Emperor said, "To present good counsel and accept admonition is what a tutor's office properly does—this is not for you to understand."
translations.idiomatic: Heshen envied him; when the succession rites were completed Gui presented a eulogy booklet and was criticized for it; the Qianlong Emperor said, "To present good counsel and accept admonition is a tutor's proper duty—this is not for you to understand."

sentences.zh: 會大學士缺，詔召珪，卒為和珅所沮。

translations.literal: When a Grand Secretary post fell vacant, an edict summoned Gui, but in the end Heshen blocked it.
translations.idiomatic: When a Grand Secretary post fell vacant, an edict summoned Gui, but Heshen blocked it in the end.

sentences.zh: 以廣東艇匪擾劫閩、浙，責珪不能緝捕，寢前命，左遷安徽巡撫。

translations.literal: Because Guangdong boat bandits harassed and plundered Fujian and Zhejiang, Gui was blamed for failing to capture them; the earlier order was set aside and he was demoted to governor of Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Because Guangdong boat bandits raided Fujian and Zhejiang, Gui was blamed for failing to capture them; the earlier order was set aside and he was demoted to governor of Anhui.

sentences.zh: 皖北复災，親治賑，官吏無侵蝕。

translations.literal: Northern Anhui suffered disaster again; he personally managed relief, and officials did not embezzle.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Anhui suffered disaster again; he personally managed relief, and officials did not embezzle.

sentences.zh: 三省教匪起，安徽亦多伏莽。

translations.literal: When sect rebels rose in the three provinces, Anhui also had many hidden desperadoes.
translations.idiomatic: When sect rebels rose in the three provinces, Anhui also had many hidden desperadoes.

sentences.zh: 珪曰：「疑而索之，是激之變。」

translations.literal: Gui said, "To suspect and search for them is to provoke rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: Gui said, "To suspect people and hunt them down is to provoke rebellion."

sentences.zh: 親駐界上籌防禦，遍蒞潁、亳所屬，集鄉老教誡之，民感化，境內迄無事。

translations.literal: He personally stationed on the border to plan defense, went everywhere through the districts under Ying and Bo, gathered village elders to instruct them, the people were moved to reform, and within the jurisdiction there was no trouble to the end.
translations.idiomatic: He personally stationed on the border to plan defense, went throughout the districts under Ying and Bo, gathered village elders to instruct them, won the people over, and kept the province peaceful.

sentences.zh: 明年，授兵部尚書，調吏部，仍留巡撫任。

translations.literal: The following year he was appointed minister of war, transferred to the Board of Personnel, and still retained the governorship.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made minister of war, transferred to the Board of Personnel, and still retained the governorship.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，高宗崩，仁宗即馳驛召珪，聞命奔赴。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year the Gaozong Emperor died; the Renzong Emperor at once sent post-horses to summon Gui; on hearing the order he rushed to obey.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of 1799 the Qianlong Emperor died; the Jiaqing Emperor at once sent post-horses to summon Gui; on hearing the order he rushed to obey.

sentences.zh: 途中上疏，略曰：「天子之孝，以繼志述事為大。

translations.literal: En route he submitted a memorial saying in summary: "The Son of Heaven's filial piety lies chiefly in continuing the late emperor's will and carrying forward his undertakings.
translations.idiomatic: En route he memorialized in summary: "The Son of Heaven's filial piety lies chiefly in continuing the late emperor's will and carrying forward his undertakings.

sentences.zh: 親政伊始，遠聽近瞻，默運乾綱，雱施渙號。

translations.literal: At the outset of personal rule, listen far and look near, silently wield the heavenly net, and pour forth edicts like rain.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset of personal rule, listen far and look near, silently wield imperial authority, and pour forth edicts like rain.

sentences.zh: 陽剛之氣，如日重光，惻怛之仁，無幽不浹。

translations.literal: The yang and firm spirit, like the sun's renewed light; compassionate benevolence reaching even the darkest places.
translations.idiomatic: Let your firm, yang spirit shine like the sun renewed; let compassionate benevolence reach even the darkest corners.

sentences.zh: 修身則嚴誠欺之界，觀人則辨義利之防。

translations.literal: In cultivating the person, strictly mark the boundary between sincerity and deceit; in observing others, distinguish the barrier between righteousness and profit.
translations.idiomatic: In self-cultivation, strictly mark the boundary between sincerity and deceit; in judging others, distinguish righteousness from profit.

sentences.zh: 君心正而四維張，朝廷清而九牧肅。

translations.literal: When the ruler's mind is correct the four bonds are extended; when the court is pure the nine provinces are orderly.
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler's mind is correct the four bonds hold firm; when the court is pure the provinces are orderly.

sentences.zh: 身先節儉，崇獎清廉，自然盜賊不足平，財用不足阜。

translations.literal: Take the lead in frugality, honor and reward integrity—then naturally bandits need not be hard to pacify nor revenues hard to enrich.
translations.idiomatic: Take the lead in frugality, honor and reward integrity—then bandits will be easy to pacify and revenues easy to enrich.

sentences.zh: 惟原皇上無忘堯、舜自​​任之心，臣敢不勉行義事君之道。」

translations.literal: I only pray Your Majesty not forget the heart that takes Yao and Shun upon oneself; how dare your servant not strive to practice the way of righteous service to the ruler."
translations.idiomatic: I only pray Your Majesty not forget the heart that takes Yao and Shun upon oneself; how dare your servant not strive to serve the ruler with righteousness."

sentences.zh: 至京哭臨，上執珪手哭失聲。

translations.literal: On reaching the capital he attended the mourning audience; the emperor took Gui's hand and wept aloud.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the capital he attended the mourning audience; the emperor took Gui's hand and wept aloud.

sentences.zh: 命直南書房，管戶部三庫，加太子少保，賜第西華門外。

translations.literal: He was ordered to regular duty in the Southern Imperial Study, to manage the three treasuries of the Board of Revenue, given the title Junior Vice Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and granted a residence outside the Xihua Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to regular duty in the Southern Imperial Study, to manage the three treasuries of the Board of Revenue, made Junior Vice Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and granted a residence outside the Xihua Gate.

sentences.zh: 時召獨對，用人行政悉以諮之。

translations.literal: He was frequently summoned for private audience; in appointments and administration everything was consulted with him.
translations.idiomatic: He was frequently summoned for private audience; appointments and administration were all consulted with him.

sentences.zh: 珪造膝密陳，不關白軍機大臣，不沽恩市直，上傾心一聽，初政之美，多出贊助。

translations.literal: Gui spoke confidentially knee to knee, did not inform the Grand Councilors, and did not curry favor by open display; the emperor listened with full trust—the beauty of the early reign owed much to his assistance.
translations.idiomatic: Gui spoke confidentially knee to knee, did not inform the Grand Councilors, and did not curry favor openly; the emperor listened with full trust—the beauty of the early reign owed much to his assistance.

sentences.zh: 尋充上書房總師傅，調戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he served as chief tutor of the Upper Imperial Study and was transferred to minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he served as chief tutor of the Upper Imperial Study and was made minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 詔清漕政，禁浮收​​。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the grain-transport system cleared up and excess collection forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the grain-transport system cleared up and excess collection forbidden.

sentences.zh: 疆吏以運丁苦累，仰給州縣，州縣不得不取諸民，於是安徽加贈銀，江蘇加耗米，珪謂小民未見清漕之益，先受其害，力爭罷之，令曹司凡事近加賦者皆議駁。

translations.literal: Frontier officials said transport laborers suffered hardship and depended on districts and counties, which had to take from the people—thus Anhui added gift silver and Jiangsu added wastage grain; Gui said the common people had not yet seen the benefit of clearing the transport system but already suffered harm, contended vigorously to abolish these, and ordered subordinate offices to reject every proposal nearing extra levy.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier officials said transport laborers suffered hardship and depended on districts and counties, which had to take from the people—thus Anhui added gift silver and Jiangsu added wastage grain; Gui said the common people had not yet seen the benefit of reforming transport but already suffered harm, fought vigorously to abolish these, and ordered subordinate offices to reject every proposal for extra levies.

sentences.zh: 長蘆鹽政請加增鹽價，駁曰：「蘆東因錢價賤，已三加價矣，且免積欠三百六十萬兩，餘欠展三年，商力已寬，無庸再議加價。」

translations.literal: The Changlu salt administration requested an increase in salt price; he rejected it, saying, "In eastern Lu, because coin was cheap, the price has already been raised three times; moreover accumulated arrears of 3,600,000 taels were remitted and remaining arrears extended three years—the merchants' capacity is already eased; there is no need to discuss raising the price again."
translations.idiomatic: The Changlu salt administration requested a salt-price increase; he rejected it, saying, "In eastern Lu, because coin was cheap, the price has already been raised three times; moreover accumulated arrears of 3,600,000 taels were remitted and remaining arrears extended three years—the merchants are already eased; there is no need to raise the price again."

sentences.zh: 廣東請濱海沙地升賦，駁曰：「海沙淤地，坍漲靡常，故照下則減半賦之。

translations.literal: Guangdong requested raising the assessment on coastal sand land; he rejected it, saying, "Sea-sand silt land shifts and subsides without constancy; therefore it is assessed at half the lowest rate.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdong requested raising the assessment on coastal sand land; he rejected it, saying, "Sea-sand silt land shifts and subsides without constancy; therefore it is assessed at half the lowest rate.

sentences.zh: 今視上、中田增賦，是與民計微利，非政體。

translations.literal: To raise the assessment now to that of upper and middle fields is to wring petty profit from the people—not proper governance.
translations.idiomatic: To raise the assessment now to that of upper and middle fields is to wring petty profit from the people—not proper governance.

sentences.zh: 且民苦加賦，別有漲地，將不敢報墾，不可行。」

translations.literal: Moreover, if the people suffer from added levies and there is separate land subject to increase, they will not dare report newly reclaimed fields—this cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, if the people suffer added levies and separate assessments on rising land, they will not dare report new reclamation—this cannot be allowed."

sentences.zh: 倉場請預納錢糧四五十倍，準作義監生，駁曰：「國家正供有常經，名實關體要。

translations.literal: The granary administration requested advance payment of grain tax forty or fifty times over, qualifying donors as tribute students by merit; he rejected it, saying, "The state's regular revenue has fixed norms; name and reality concern the body's essentials.
translations.idiomatic: The granary administration requested advance grain-tax payment forty or fifty times over in exchange for status as tribute students by merit; he rejected it, saying, "The state's regular revenue has fixed norms; name and reality concern fundamental governance.

sentences.zh: 於名不正，實必傷，斷不可行。」

translations.literal: When the name is not correct, the reality must be harmed—this absolutely cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: When the name is not correct, the reality must suffer—this absolutely cannot be allowed."

sentences.zh: 凡駁議每自屬稿，奏上，皆韙之。

translations.literal: In every rejection he drafted the text himself; when memorialized upward, all were approved.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted every rejection himself; when memorialized upward, all were approved.

sentences.zh: 五年，兼署吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he concurrently acted as minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In 1800 he concurrently acted as minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 先是彭元瑞於西華門內墜馬，珪呼其輿入舁之，為御史週栻所劾。

translations.literal: Earlier Peng Yuanrui had fallen from his horse inside the Xihua Gate; Gui called his sedan chair inside to carry him up, and was impeached by censor Zhou Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Peng Yuanrui had fallen from his horse inside the Xihua Gate; Gui called his sedan chair inside to carry him, and censor Zhou Shi impeached him for it.

sentences.zh: 尋有珪輿人毆傷禁門兵，忌者嗾護軍統領訐之。

translations.literal: Soon Gui's sedan bearers beat and wounded a Forbidden Gate guard; enviers incited the banner guard commander to denounce him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Gui's sedan bearers beat a Forbidden Gate guard; his enemies incited the banner guard commander to denounce him.

sentences.zh: 詔：「珪素恪謹，造次不檢，特申戒。」

translations.literal: An edict said: "Gui has always been careful and respectful; in a moment of carelessness he was not restrained—he is specially admonished."
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Gui has always been careful and respectful; in a moment of carelessness he was not restrained—he is specially admonished."

sentences.zh: 坐褫宮銜，解三庫事，鐫級留任。

translations.literal: He was punished by stripping of palace rank, relieved of the three treasuries, reduced in grade, and kept in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was stripped of palace rank, relieved of the three treasuries, reduced in grade, and kept in office.

sentences.zh: 七年，協辦大學士，复太子少保。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he served as associate Grand Secretary and was restored as Junior Vice Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In 1802 he served as associate Grand Secretary and was restored as Junior Vice Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 尋兼翰林院掌院學士，晉太子少傅。

translations.literal: Soon he concurrently served as chancellor of the Hanlin Academy and was promoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he also served as chancellor of the Hanlin Academy and was promoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 九年，上幸翰林院，聯句賜宴，御書「天祿儲才」額刻懸院中，以墨書賜珪家。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the emperor visited the Hanlin Academy, gave a linked-verse banquet, and had the imperial inscription "Heaven's Blessings Store Talent" carved and hung in the academy; ink writing was bestowed on Gui's family.
translations.idiomatic: In 1804 the emperor visited the Hanlin Academy, gave a linked-verse banquet, and had the imperial inscription "Heaven's Blessings Store Talent" carved and hung in the academy; an ink inscription was bestowed on Gui's family.

sentences.zh: 十年，拜體仁閣大學士，管理工部。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was made Grand Secretary of the Hall of Embodied Benevolence and put in charge of the Board of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In 1805 he was made Grand Secretary of the Hall of Embodied Benevolence and put in charge of the Board of Works.

sentences.zh: 上以是命遵高宗諭，遣詣裕陵謝。

translations.literal: Because this appointment followed the Gaozong Emperor's instruction, the emperor sent him to the Yuling mausoleum to give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Because this appointment followed the Qianlong Emperor's instruction, the emperor sent him to the Yuling mausoleum to give thanks.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，年七十六，以老乞休，溫詔慰留，賜玉鳩杖；

translations.literal: After a year, at seventy-six, citing age he begged to retire; a warm edict comforted him and kept him on, granting a jade dove staff;
translations.idiomatic: After a year, at seventy-six, he asked to retire citing age; a warm edict urged him to stay and granted him a jade dove staff;

sentences.zh: 命天寒，間二三日入直。
