translations.literal: he was ordered that in cold weather he need enter regular duty only every two or three days.
translations.idiomatic: and ordered that in cold weather he need enter regular duty only every two or three days.

sentences.zh: 未幾，召對乾清宮，眩暈，扶歸第，數日卒。

translations.literal: Before long, summoned for audience in the Palace of Heavenly Purity, he grew dizzy, was helped back to his residence, and died within several days.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, summoned for audience in the Palace of Heavenly Purity, he grew dizzy, was helped home, and died within several days.

sentences.zh: 上親奠，哭之慟。

translations.literal: The emperor personally offered libations and wept with deep grief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally offered libations and wept with deep grief.

sentences.zh: 贈太傅，祀賢良祠，賜金治喪。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given the title Grand Tutor, enshrined in the Shrine of Worthies, and granted gold for the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made Grand Tutor, enshrined in the Shrine of Worthies, and granted gold for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 詔：「珪自為師傅，凡所陳說，無非唐、虞、三代之言，稍涉時趨者不出諸口，啟沃至多。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Since Gui became tutor, everything he stated was nothing but the words of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties; what slightly touched current fashion never left his mouth—his counsel was abundant.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Since Gui became tutor, everything he said was the language of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties; what touched current fashion never left his mouth—his counsel was abundant.

sentences.zh: 揆諸諡法，足當'正'字而無愧，特諡文正。

translations.literal: Measured against posthumous naming standards, he fully merits the character 'correct' without shame; he was specially given the posthumous name Wenzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Measured against posthumous naming standards, he fully merits the character for 'correct' without shame; he was specially given the posthumous name Wenzheng.

sentences.zh: 又見其門庭卑隘，清寒之況，不減儒素。」

translations.literal: Moreover, seeing his gate and courtyard low and narrow, his condition of clean poverty was no less than that of a plain scholar."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, seeing his gate and courtyard low and narrow, his plain poverty was no less than that of a scholar of modest means."

sentences.zh: 命內府備筵，遣皇子加奠。

translations.literal: He ordered the inner palace to prepare a feast and sent a prince to offer additional libations.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the inner palace to prepare a feast and sent a prince to offer additional libations.

sentences.zh: 啟殯日，遣慶郡王永璘祖奠目送。

translations.literal: On the day the coffin was opened for burial, Prince Yonglin of Qing was sent to offer ancestral libations and see him off with his eyes.
translations.idiomatic: On the day the coffin was opened for burial, Prince Yonglin of Qing was sent to offer ancestral libations and see him off.

sentences.zh: 逾年，上謁西陵，珪墓近蹕路，遣官賜奠。

translations.literal: After a year, when the emperor visited the Western Tombs, Gui's tomb was near the imperial route; an official was sent to grant libations.
translations.idiomatic: After a year, when the emperor visited the Western Tombs, Gui's tomb lay near the imperial route; an official was sent to offer libations.

sentences.zh: 高宗實錄成，特賜祭，擢長子錫經為四品京堂。

translations.literal: When the Gaozong Emperor's Veritable Records were completed, sacrificial rites were specially granted and his eldest son Xijing was promoted to fourth-rank capital office.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qianlong Veritable Records were completed, sacrificial rites were specially granted and his eldest son Xijing was promoted to fourth-rank capital office.

sentences.zh: 二十年，復因謁陵回鑾，親奠其墓，恩禮始終無與比。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, again on returning from tomb visitation, he personally offered libations at the tomb—favor from start to finish had no equal.
translations.idiomatic: In 1815, again on returning from tomb visitation, he personally offered libations at the tomb—favor from start to finish had no equal.

sentences.zh: 珪文章奧博，取士重經策，銳意求才。

translations.literal: Gui's writings were profound and broad; in selecting scholars he stressed classical examinations and policy essays, and keenly sought talent.
translations.idiomatic: Gui's writings were profound and broad; in selecting scholars he stressed classical examinations and policy essays and keenly sought talent.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年典會試，阮元佐之，一時名流搜拔殆盡，為士林宗仰者數十年。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing he presided over the metropolitan examination with Ruan Yuan assisting; eminent men of the time were sought and raised almost to exhaustion, and for decades he was revered by the scholarly community.
translations.idiomatic: In 1799 he presided over the metropolitan examination with Ruan Yuan assisting; eminent men of the time were sought and raised almost to exhaustion, and for decades he was revered by the scholarly community.

sentences.zh: 學無不通，亦喜道家，嘗曰：「硃子注參同契，非空言也。」

translations.literal: In learning nothing was closed to him; he also delighted in Daoism and once said, "Zhu Xi's commentary on the Cantong qi is not empty talk."
translations.idiomatic: In learning nothing was closed to him; he also delighted in Daoism and once said, "Zhu Xi's commentary on the Cantong qi is not empty talk."

sentences.zh: 論曰：君子小人消長之機，國運系焉。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: The mechanism by which gentlemen and petty men wax and wane is where the nation's fortune lies.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal says: The rise and fall of gentlemen and petty men is where the nation's fortune lies.

sentences.zh: 王杰、董誥、硃珪皆高宗拔擢信任之臣，和珅一再間沮，卒不屈撓。

translations.literal: Wang Jie, Dong Gao, and Zhu Gui were all ministers the Gaozong Emperor selected and trusted; Heshen repeatedly obstructed them between, yet in the end they did not yield or bend.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jie, Dong Gao, and Zhu Gui were all ministers the Qianlong Emperor selected and trusted; Heshen repeatedly obstructed them, yet in the end they did not yield.

sentences.zh: 一旦共、驩伏法，眾正盈朝，攄其忠誠，啟沃新主，殄寇息民，苞桑永固。

translations.literal: Once Gong and Huan were executed by law—the names by which Heshen is here indicated—the upright filled the court; they poured forth their loyalty, nourished the new sovereign, exterminated bandits and gave the people rest, and the nation was firmly secured like mulberry roots in earth.
translations.idiomatic: Once Heshen was executed, the upright filled the court; they poured forth their loyalty, nourished the new sovereign, exterminated bandits and gave the people rest, and secured the realm like deep-rooted mulberry.

sentences.zh: 天留數人，弼成仁宗初政之盛，可謂大臣矣。

translations.literal: Heaven left a few such men to assist and complete the splendor of the Renzong Emperor's early reign—they may be called great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven left a few such men to assist and complete the splendor of the Jiaqing Emperor's early reign—they may truly be called great ministers.
